author: claude

patch.value: A case opener sharing its first arm cleared the outer scope and refused a genuinely attested publish

The sibling-arm reset that closed the case-arm bypass ran before the block scope was pushed. A case opener that shares a segment with its first arm both opens the block and starts an arm, so the reset cleared the parent scope instead of a fresh arm scope. A flag bound before the block became unresolvable and the auditor refused a publish that carries provenance on every path, which would block a release check.

A binding made before a case block survives an opener that shares its first arm; A binding made inside a case arm still cannot attest a publish after esac; Both are verified red on revert in the correct direction

message: Record the over-refusal introduced by the case-arm fix

value.author: claude
value.text:
Reproduced and fixed. Before: 'FLAG=--provenance; case $X in a) : ;; esac; npm publish $FLAG' was refused although FLAG is --provenance on every path. The multi-line spelling of the same shape was accepted, which localised the defect to the opener sharing a segment with its first arm.

Fix: the arm reset now runs only when the segment does not itself open a scope. When it does open one, the scope pushed immediately afterwards is already empty, which is the same branch identity by construction, so clearing beforehand could only reach the outer scope.

Red-on-revert, in both directions. Removing the change <= 0 guard turns 'a binding made before a case block survives an opener that shares its first arm' red while 'a binding made inside a case arm still cannot attest a publish after esac' stays green. That pairing is the point: the second test is what proves the fix did not reopen the bypass the reset exists to close, and a fix that only made the first test green would be a regression.

Full sixteen-case matrix after the change: eight fail-opens still refused, eight legitimate constructions still accepted, zero mismatches. Fleet scan unchanged at 21 OK with pm-rust recognition none.

patch.value: Arm reset deferred so a case opener sharing its first arm no longer clears the outer scope; the arm-local bypass stays closed, verified red on revert in both directions.
